sentence: 42-year-old male patient who came to the emergency room after suffering a bruise to his left eye.
The patient had previously undergone phacoemulsification of the lens, with intraocular lens implantation; He subsequently underwent a vitrectomy for retinal detachment.
Maintaining visual acuity after the intervention of 2/10.
During the ophthalmological examination, the visual acuity of the right eye was 10/10 and the perception and projection of light was 10/10 in the left.

Biomicroscopically; In the left eye, moderate hyphema, significant dialysis of the iris with pupillary involvement, Descemet's folds, and extreme hypotonia of the eyeball were notable (later confirmed with applanation tonometry, which showed ocular tension at values ​​close to zero).
The fundus examination revealed a massive hemovitreum that made it impossible to visualize the retina.
After ruling out a previous penetrating injury, a diagnosis of suspected posterior scleral rupture was made and confirmed by an orbital computed tomography (CT) scan.
Given the situation of the balloon, the patient was admitted; and observation was indicated due to the high risk of massive expulsive suprachoroidal hemorrhage if he underwent surgery1.
Antibiotic and corticosteroid treatment was prescribed; carrying out exhaustive monitoring of the affected eye and the olephrum, as there are possibilities of developing sympathetic ophthalmia.

After two weeks, there was an improvement in visual acuity that went from perceiving and projecting light to lumps, with a recovery of the structure of the eyeball; which was confirmed with a new orbital CT scan, observing a sealed posterior leak point, compatible with reconstitution.
After a few months of control, there was progressive resorption of the hemovitreal, finding a significant scar choroidal rupture.
This did not lead to an improvement in visual acuity, due to macular and optic nerve involvement.

In this case, at first we considered a massive ocular burst due to the initial CT image, but later, we thought if what really happened was a massive hyperpressure that compressed the eyeball giving the tomographic image and later, when the break was sealed, the he recovered his constitution; The fact that the balloon was vitrectomized contributed to all this.
